python_unchanged.rule: A request without target, or with target python, returns the same bytes as the accepted compiler-v1 default for the same request. No existing CNL text, typed prompt, bundle, asset or Python output changes.
checks: All 127 public Python products are byte-identical to their accepted outputs.
All 544 historical jobs keep their accepted results.
The legacy 100 and 214 case sets keep their scope.
Every negative case python_control_body gives its python_control_expected result (tests/rust-output-v1/check_python_controls.py).
Every coverage case gives the same Python bundle payload_sha256 and Python file hashes as the frozen evidence (tests/rust-output-v1/validate_cases.py).

target_selection_checks: Every target-examples.json body gives its expected result.
Every RT case gives exactly its expected diagnostic, located in the raw request body.
A target python request gives the same bytes as the request without target, for every acceptance case and every CNL positive fixture.
The CLI forwards --target unchanged and exits with status 2 on a refusal.
scope_checks: Every RS and RP case gives exactly its expected diagnostic with target rust.
Every out-of-scope public example, CNL positive fixture and legacy job gives UNSUPPORTED_TARGET with the refusal case-inventory.json records for it, with target rust.
The compiler refusal for each case equals tests/rust-output-v1/rust_profile.py on the typed prompt.
bundle_checks: For every acceptance case, the CNL and typed JSON requests with target rust return byte-identical som.dsl-bundle.v2 bundles.
Every Rust bundle validates against bundle.schema.json, has at most 12 files and 64 blocks, and every block id starts with rust.
Two compiles and two assembles of the same request give the same bytes.
The assembled files are exactly the product-layout.json file set, and Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock equal the reference files.

assemble_refusals.base: A valid Rust bundle for the acceptance case example-v1, and for A6 the bundle for example-v5.
assemble_refusals.rehash: Unless a recipe says otherwise, recompute prompt_sha256, dsl_sha256 and payload_sha256 with the frozen formulas after the change, so the hash check passes and the named check is reached.
assemble_refusals.span: Line, column and byte spans locate the pointer target in the canonical assemble request body, computed at test time.

Replace catalog, block_library, backend and formatter with the Python descriptors from the compiler-v1 manifest.
Add target rust to a valid som.dsl-bundle.v1 Python bundle.

each_acceptance_case: cargo test --locked --offline -- --test-threads=1 with TEST_DATABASE_URL on a fresh database; a missing database is a failure
schema equivalence with the Python migration for the same prompt (behavior-normalization.json)
the behavior parity suite against the Python product for the same prompt, after the frozen normalization
the strict refusals in behavior-normalization.json divergences D1 to D5 checked on the Rust product alone
product_gates.no_sampling: Every acceptance case runs every gate. A missing result, a failure and a skipped check are each reported as such and block acceptance.

amendments: After the freeze receipt is sealed, a change to any frozen file is a numbered amendment with its reason, the old and new hashes, and an independent review.
